title: An error in the first line is refused without keeping memory in proportion to the 64 MiB that follows
notes: The first line is `a: b: c`. The value of a block mapping entry cannot start another block mapping on the same line (section 8.2.2, [194]), and a plain scalar cannot contain `: ` ([130]), so the document is invalid at the second colon (line 1, column 5); yaml-test-suite ZCZ6 is the same mistake. What follows is 22,369,618 lines of `x:`, 64 MiB in all. The answer is a syntax error. A limit error is accepted as a resource refusal (a library configured with an input-size cap refuses 64 MiB before it reads it); it is not a second answer of the specification. Bounds. Memory: 1536 MB, 24 times the input. The kit measures the whole adapter process, and delivering a 64 MiB input already costs the adapter several times that before the library is called (base64 text, decoded bytes, and UTF-16 strings in some runtimes): 4.9 times in Go, 3.7 times in Rust, up to 16.4 times in .NET, so the room left for the library differs by language. A reader that tokenizes the whole input before reporting the error keeps 28 times the input or more. Storage that is reserved but never touched is not seen, because the kit reads resident memory. Time: 150 seconds, a hang guard, not a measure of cost. A linear read of the whole input at the rate of the sibling safety/ten-million-digit-plain-scalar-events (0.2 seconds per megabyte) takes about 13 seconds, so a reader that is slower than linear but finishes inside 150 seconds passes on time; the time limit catches only a hang, and the memory bound is what separates readers that read everything before reporting the error. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The input is generated from the recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md); fast mode leaves this case out (tag slow).

provenance.reference: A reader that tokenized the whole input, keeping a token for every few bytes, before it reported an error in the first line: 38 times the input on 64 MiB.
